questions.q: What does the Dolly Varden trout do when food is scarce?
a: It shrinks its digestive organs and slows digestion
It migrates to warmer waters for the season
It stores extra fat under its scales
It stops reproducing for several years
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the fish to show that saving should flex with circumstances.

questions.q: What saving approach does the author recommend instead of a fixed rate?
a: Save more when income is high and less when it is low
Save the same percentage no matter what happens
Save nothing until you are close to retirement
Save only windfalls and annual bonuses
questions.why: Lesson 1 says save what you can, when you can, rather than forcing a set rate.

questions.q: Why does the summary favor earning more over cutting costs?
a: Your capacity to earn is nearly unlimited, unlike spending cuts
Higher income always lowers the taxes you owe
Cutting costs never improves anyone's savings
Employers reward people who spend less money
questions.why: Lesson 2 says saving potential is limited but earning capacity is nearly infinite.

questions.q: What does just keep buying refer to in the summary?
a: Continuing to buy broad stock market funds over time
Buying a home as soon as you can afford one
Purchasing shares of individual companies you like
Spending freely on things that bring you joy
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it means steadily buying broad market ETFs to build portfolio income.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is money's real question for us?
a: What matters most to us, so money goes to the right things
How much of each paycheck should be invested
Which bank offers the highest interest rate
When should you retire and stop working
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the challenge is identifying priorities, not just save-versus-spend ratios.
